text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS @

- At the meeting of the coalition consultative council yesterday party leaders agreed on the need to expand the forums of cooperation between the two parties. Socialist caucus leader Imre Szekeres said there is no coalition crisis as the Free Democrats have taken note of the fact that the Socialists prefer to have a minister for privatisation.
- President Arpad Goncz opened talks with President Suleyman Demirel on Turkey in Ankara on Wednesday.
- Parliament resumed debate on a conflict of interest bill pertaining to MPs and opened a debate on amending the law on VAT and consumption tax. @

- Marta Tocsik is unlikely to repay any of the commission she has received from the State Privatisation and Holding Co. (APV) unless her HUF 804 million contract is invalidated by a court, her defence attorney said.
- Due to an increase in both exports and consumption, 1997 may see a 2.5 percent rise in GDP, according to a study by the economic research firm GKI.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs and his Cypriot counterpart signed a cooperation pact yesterday. @
- Ivan Peto, President of the Free Democrats said in an interview that he did not simply offer to resign but actually tendered his resignation Monday night.
NEPSZAVA

- Data protection ombudsman Laszlo Majthenyi has launched an investigation into why the documents on the forthcoming trial over the Gabcikovo-Nagymaros hydropower plant and the diverting of the Danube by Slovakia are classified as secret.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Board of Directors of the International Energy Agency has decided yesterday to invite Hungary among its members. @
- The BUX Index reached another record high value yesterday, breaking the 3,700 mark for the first time.
- The European Investment Bank will join the consortium extending a $175 million loan to the mobile phone company Pannon GSM.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy emphasized private sector growth in an assessment of Hungary's economic prospects for 1997 in an interview.
- In accordance with expectations, treasury bill yields are stabilising, a trend reinforced at Tuesday's auction. @
- The last large package of bad debts and real estate originally belonging to Magyar Hitel Bank was sold Monday to Gordius Holding Rt.
- Citibank Budapest Rt., a subsidiary of the US-based Citicorp, boosted revenues by 20-30 percent in the first nine months of the year compared to the same period in 1995.

- Hungarian institutional investors bought 15 percent of the share package in the chemical company BorsodChem during the recent closed issue. British institutions acquired almost 80 percent of the tranche before the issue closed October 11. @
- A woman who allowed George Soros and his mother to hide in her house in 1944 recently asked the businessman for funds to finance a school and received HUF 40 million.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Retail trade and catering revenues in August were 5.6 percent and 1.4 percent below those in the same month last year.
- Shares of the mineral water bottling company Kekkut may appear on the stock exchange next month.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
